conditions.text: Sample charges assume a recipient of similar alignment and religion requesting service at the cleric’s headquarters. Prices may be adjusted for faithful lower-level characters and raised for nonregular attendees. Travel without risk can raise charges as much as double; when at risk a cleric is likely to refuse or charge at least five times the rates. Attack spells are not listed; as a general rule specially hired spellcasters do not accompany adventures except when planned and directed by the DM.

Ditch 100 ft by 10 ft deep by 20 ft wide assumes 3–4 workers for six weeks; heavy clay doubles time. Stone fortress construction takes about one week per 10-ft cubic section; adding 50% to expenditure doubles the rate, while triple rate requires expenditure of 250% of base cost and is the stated maximum. Listed normal stone buildings take four months. Building materials are assumed on hand; quarrying, transport and architect costs are additional. Wooden buildings take about half the time of comparable stone buildings.

The stone building’s listed price includes one 1-ft stone course, 120 ft of outside walls 20 ft high, two wooden floors, two flights of stairs, roof and one wooden door; cellar excavation, ground flooring, windows, interior walls and extra doors cost extra. Each additional 1-ft course adds 10% of initial cost. A 10-ft-thick example is 500 gp plus 90%, or 950 gp. An earth rampart immediately above one side of a ditch costs 20% of the listed rampart amount.

Iron door: add or subtract 2 gp per square foot of half-inch iron altered. Secret door: no reduction for smaller portals; larger ones add 5 gp per square foot of increased size. Trap door: each additional square foot costs 1 sp. Wooden door: one square foot of added or reduced wood is 2 sp. Reinforced wooden door: each square foot alteration is 5 sp. Drawbridge: each square foot alteration is valued at 2 gp. Portcullis: adjust cost by 2 gp per square foot alteration.
The stated tunnel is dug through soft earth and floored, walled and roofed in rough stone. Hard earth increases cost by 100%; solid rock costs 500% of the listed figure.
Ballista missile cost is comparable to javelin cost; the source does not give a separate fixed price in this passage.

The listed receptacle figures are suggested costs. A specially blessed/cursed empty crystal or special leaded-glass vial is worth 2–5 gp. Combination-metal vessel capacity may be interpolated: the printed half-copper, half-silver example holds 8 vials and costs 50% of each vessel price. Fonts and basins require special order and take 4–10 (2d4+2) weeks. A defiled font/basin is smelted and remade at 20%–50% of normal figures, taking 4–6 weeks.
